The largest electromagnetic force in the melt appears near the solid-liquid interface, and there is an electromagnetic force gradient in front of the interface.
The PMF generates periodic electromagnetic compressive and pull forces in the melt, with the compressive force being about ten times larger than the pull force.
The electromagnetic vibration is more intensive ahead of the solidification front when considering the solid-liquid interface.
The forced convection is concentrated in front of the solid-liquid interface, leading to a more uniform temperature distribution and a lower temperature gradient.
The flow velocity in front of the solid-liquid interface along the thermal gradient is greater than 2 mm/s, which is higher than the speed of the isotherms (0.75 mm/s).
The application of the PMF changes the solidification structure of the superalloy K4169 from coarse columnar grains to fine equiaxed grains.
The Joule heat is mainly concentrated near the surface of the sample due to the skin effect, and the Joule heat in the solid phase is significantly higher than that in the liquid phase.
The flow field is stable, but the flow velocity increases slightly as the volume of the liquid phase decreases during directional solidification.
The criterion for dendrite fragmentation is that the component of flow velocity along the thermal gradient should be larger than the speed of the isotherms, which is the case in the present study.
The electromagnetic vibration and the forced convection in front of the solid-liquid interface are the main reasons for the grain refinement under the PMF.
The PMF generates periodic positive and negative pressure in the melt, leading to the vibration of the melt.
The induced current in the solid phase is approximately twice that of the liquid phase, although the resistance of the solid phase is half that of the liquid phase.
The direction of the net force imposed on the melt changes periodically, which further proves that the melt is subjected to periodic pressure and pulling force.
The flow pattern of the melt caused by the PMF is laminar, with a Reynolds number of about 57.
The curvature of the solid-liquid interface decreases with the application of the PMF, as confirmed by the simulation results and the liquid metal quenching experiments.
